name: 魏暘
objective:
“Biomimetic Engineering” is a kind of knowledge transferring from biology to
engineering technology. After billions of years of evolution, it has been proven
that the biological system is highly efficient and sustainable. In this course, the
latest progress in Biomimetic Engineering will be introduced. It will bring us
revolutionary breakthroughs if we learn from nature and apply it to technology.
The topics covered in this course will include (1) an introduction to
bioinspiration, (2) biofabrication, (3) biomacromolecules, and (4) biomaterials
and their application in bioinspired engineering.
schedule:
Week1 Introduction to Biological (Natural) Materials
Week2 Basic Building Blocks: Amino acid, proteins, polysaccharides, lipids,
minerals
Week3 Cells: structure and functions
Week4 Bio-mineralization
Week5 Silicate-based Composites: Diatoms, sea sponges
Week6 Calcium carbonate-based Composite: Mollusk shells, crustacean
exoskeletons
Week7 Calcium phosphate-based Composite: Bone and teeth
Week8 Biological Polymers and Polymer-based Composites
Week9 midterm report
Week10 Cellular Solids (Foams)
Week11 Functional Biological Materials I: Adhesion and attachment
Week12 Functional Biological Materials II: Surface properties
Week13 Functional Biological Materials III: Optical properties
Week14 Bio-inspired and biomimetic materials: engineering approaches
Week15 Molecular-based Biomimetic
Week16-19 Final Presentation/Project
scorePolicy:
1. Class performance/absence 40%
2. Regular reports 50%
3. Final reports 10%
*This course involves extensive discussions and research presentations, and students who enroll must be engaged in biomaterials-related research.
materials: Biological Materials Science: Biological Materials, Bio-inspired Materials and Biomaterials/ M.A. Meyers and P.-Y. Chen. Cambridge University Press. 2014. pp1.630.
